tag: [C] arithmetic on published-typical input prices [E] — NOT a DOC model. KESTREL-X1 is HYBRID-electric (turbo-generators burn fuel, battery is a buffer); the battery-electric comparison below is the all-electric bound.

inputs_E.note: typical published values, ranges in comments — verify before citing

verdict: At $0.10/kWh grid power, battery-electric energy costs 1.37x jet fuel per mission — NOT cheaper on energy alone [C]. Electric wins on energy price only below $0.073/kWh (off-peak / renewables). The honest case for the hybrid-electric layout is emissions, noise, and maintenance — plus the ~48x mass penalty per kWh is why full battery-electric is hard for a 1,500 nm mission. 'Cheap' is therefore a [T] target with conditions, not a result.
caveats: Energy price only — excludes maintenance, engine overhaul, battery replacement cycles, and carbon pricing, which can flip the comparison (published direction: electric wins more as carbon prices rise) [E, verify].
KESTREL-X1 as configured is hybrid-electric: the 2 turbo-generators burn Jet A; the battery is a takeoff/climb buffer, so its mission energy is mostly jet fuel today.
Prices are point values with ranges in comments; recompute with current prices before any real use.
